title: Dashboards Are Dead — Sarah Simionescu, Composio
talk_summary: A Composio engineer argues dashboards are obsolete because agents, not humans, are the new users, and that raw MCP servers fail agents due to no memory, context bloat from tool definitions, and per-app isolation. Their fix is a 'search-then-plan' meta-tool that returns only the relevant tools plus a usage plan, plus remote workbench execution that keeps large data out of context.

takeaways.technique: Tool search + plan instead of loading all tool definitions
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent first calls a single 'search' tool stating its sub-tasks; the service returns only the matching tools plus a step-by-step plan for using them, instead of dumping every tool schema into context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it calls composio search to state the task it wants to accomplish... returns not only the correct tools it needs, but actually a plan of how to use them
takeaways.numbers: GitHub toolkit alone has over 200 tools

takeaways.technique: Keep bulk data out of the context window
takeaways.what_they_do: Intermediate results (user IDs, query outputs) are saved to a workbench and referenced, not loaded into context; the agent generates a query against the saved data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it actually saves it without loading the full results into its context... without ever loading the entire thing into its context window

takeaways.technique: Cross-app task decomposition with per-source plans
takeaways.what_they_do: One agent decomposes a task into per-source sub-goals (Slack, Sentry, Datadog), fetches each source's plan, then executes data pulls in parallel before scanning code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it begins pulling from data sources in parallel. Data dog sentry and it begins scanning the codebase
takeaways.numbers: PR with a fix in less than five minutes

takeaways.technique: Return usage plans with tools, not just schemas
takeaways.what_they_do: Tool responses include ordering/dependency guidance (e.g., resolve channel ID before querying messages), so the model doesn't have to rediscover prerequisites each run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for Slack, you actually have to find the Slack channel ID before you can start quering for messages

takeaways.technique: Design interfaces for agents, not humans
takeaways.what_they_do: They wrap messy, changing third-party APIs into a unified agent-facing interface rather than exposing each app's native surface.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We translate messy, sparsely documented, everchanging APIs... into something that agents really love to use
